svg.title: Research Platform end-to-end system flow
svg.desc: End-to-end infrastructure view. Four client surfaces -- the control panel running natively on the host, telegram-bot, mcp-gateway and langflow -- reach the API, which puts the run on the arq queue; CapacityGate measures free VRAM and hands out a slot to the worker, and the scheduler can preempt a running job for an urgent one. The worker is drawn as one box and fans out to five things: 27 external connectors, crawl4ai, the in-process SmartPdfParser, the agentsearch adapter and Ollama on the host. PDFs go through a fast path, a heavy re-extraction of only the flagged pages, and a merge with quarantine checks, then land in postgres and minio and are delivered back to the surfaces as bundles. Three strips across the bottom summarise image topology, the single shared GPU, and the identity layer.
svg.text: 3 · WHAT THE WORKER CALLS OUT TO
personal rp_ key · no shared token
hands out run slots in priority order
an urgent run pauses the running one
resumes it where it left off
connector errors are silent: the run goes on
that container is OUTSIDE this compose project
off -> fast-path text kept, doc degraded
profile suffix records how it was produced
docker compose down -v does not erase this
back to the surfaces: .docx · report · evidence

Dockerfile (COPY src + pip install .) -> api · worker · mcp-gateway · telegram-bot · migrate · agentsearch-adapter all share ONE image (*app anchor) · Dockerfile.docling is a separate image: torch is several GB · the control panel is in no image at all

RTX 4060 8 GB: Ollama resident + docling (DOCLING_MAX_CONCURRENT=1) · CapacityGate reserves docling_vram_reserve_gb but cannot measure docling · drop the COMPOSE_FILE overlay and docling silently falls back to CPU, producing DIFFERENT text
auth.py · Principal · ownership is enforced in the Repository layer (metaclass), not in routes · rp_ API keys · SERVICE_TOKEN · SESSION_SECRET · the panel reads .env.office, not .env
The 15 pipeline nodes collapse into a single worker box — the stage-by-stage flow lives in the langgraph-state-machine diagram.
Every stage writes through Repository and leaves a _boundary() checkpoint; those writes are not drawn individually.
Focal: the process that runs the run
Control and return — preemption, SSE, delivery
